question: Why did Ceylon, once one of the world's great coffee exporters, stop growing coffee?
answer: A fungus. Coffee leaf rust, Hemileia vastatrix, was recorded on the island in 1869 and stripped plantations of their leaves year after year; within about two decades exports had collapsed. Planters uprooted the bushes and put tea on the same hillsides. The island's famous tea gardens stand on ground first cleared for coffee.
move: Behind a famous product, look for the crop it replaced and why.
reference: McCook, Coffee Is Not Forever: A Global History of the Coffee Leaf Rust, Ohio University Press, 2019
